name: Glowforge Aura
tagline: Consumer-friendly CO₂ laser with the simplest setup — at a subscription cost
tldr: Glowforge's compact CO₂ laser designed for crafters. Easy software, quick setup, and decent cutting for thin materials. The catch: premium hardware price plus required subscription for full features, and a smaller work area than xTool P2.

priceRange.note: Plus mandatory Premium subscription (~$50/mo) for full functionality

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: Easiest software experience in the category
Compact footprint for a CO₂ machine
Brand recognition helps when selling craft products
cons: Subscription required for full features — ongoing cost
Less power than desktop CO₂ machines like xTool P2
Cloud-dependent — needs internet for most jobs
beginnerNotes: Great if you hate tinkering and want to cut thin craft materials today. Bad value if you are technical and willing to learn LightBurn — an xTool D1 Pro or used K40 gives more capability per dollar.
proTips: Factor subscription cost over 2–3 years into your budget. Proofgrade materials are convenient but expensive — third-party plywood works with testing. Aura is craft-scale, not sign-shop scale.
primaryUse: Simple CO₂ cutting and engraving for crafters who prioritize ease of use over power and cost efficiency.
mainObjective: Easiest CO₂ setup for crafters who want zero tinkering
